\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p061-product-open-tube}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value.  Let \(A\) and \(B\) be strict \(K\)-affinoid algebras, let
\(a\in\mathcal M(A)(K)\), and write
\[
 P=A\widehat\otimes_KB,
 \qquad
 s_a:\mathcal M(B)\longrightarrow\mathcal M(P)
\]
for the section induced by evaluation at \(a\).  If
\(z\in\mathcal M(B)\) and \(\Omega\subset\mathcal M(P)\) is an ordinary
open neighbourhood of \(s_a(z)\), then there are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods \(U\subset\mathcal M(A)\) of \(a\) and
\(V\subset\mathcal M(B)\) of \(z\) such that
\[
                         U\times_KV\subset\Omega.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}
Let \(K\) be as above, let \(N\) be a lattice, put \(M=N^\vee\), and let
\(\rho\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be a full-dimensional strongly convex
rational polyhedral cone.  Put
\[
 S=\rho^\vee\cap M,
 \qquad
 Z=\operatorname{Spec}K[S],
\]
and denote by \(a\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}(K)\) its torus-fixed point.  Let \(Y\)
be a good strict \(K\)-analytic space, let \(y\in Y\), and let
\(\Omega\) be an ordinary open neighbourhood of \((a,y)\) in
\(Z^{\mathrm{an}}\times_KY\).  For every classically pluriharmonic
function \(h:\Omega\to\mathbf R\), there are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods \(U\) of \(a\) and \(V\) of \(y\), with
\(U\times_KV\subset\Omega\), such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-parameterized-toric-factorization}
 h|_{U\times_KV}
   =p_V^*g,
 \qquad
 g=s_a^*h|_V\in\operatorname{PH}(V).
\end{equation}
The neighbourhood \(U\) can be chosen from the cofinal weighted toric
affinoids
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-parameterized-weighted-domain}
 U_n=\left\{x\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}:
  |\chi^u(x)|\leq|\varpi|^{n\langle u,v\rangle}
  \text{ for every }u\in S\right\},
\end{equation}
where \(0<|\varpi|<1\) and \(v\in N\cap\operatorname{int}(\rho)\).
In particular, if \(Y\) has the local property that every classically
pluriharmonic function is \(\mathbf R\)-PL, then the germ of \(h\) at
\((a,y)\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  This applies when \(Y\) is quasi-smooth.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let \(N\) be a lattice, and let
\(\sigma\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be any strongly convex rational
polyhedral cone, with no simpliciality or full-dimensionality assumption.
Set
\[
 X_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}
 K[\sigma^\vee\cap M],
 \qquad M=N^\vee.
\]
Every classically pluriharmonic function on an ordinary open analytic
subspace \(W\subset X_\sigma^{\mathrm{an}}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and
harmonic in the sense of Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.  Equivalently, this holds
at every analytic point of every torus orbit, including every
positive-dimensional orbit of a non-simplicial cone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties}
The conclusion of \Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits} holds on every
ordinary open analytic subspace of the analytification of a split toric
variety associated to an arbitrary fan.  It also holds on every good
strict analytic space which is analytically locally isomorphic to an
ordinary open neighbourhood of a point
\[
 (a,y)\in Z^{\mathrm{an}}\times_KY,
\]
where \(Z\) and \(a\) are as in
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre} and \(Y\) is
quasi-smooth.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-toric-forms}
Let \(X\) be a \(K\)-variety for which there is a finite analytic field
extension \(L/K\) such that \(X_L\) is a split toric \(L\)-variety.  Then
every classically pluriharmonic function on an ordinary open analytic
subspace of \(X^{\mathrm{an}}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.  In particular, the conclusion holds for
ordinary open subspaces of algebraic toric forms after any finite field
extension which splits the form.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value.  Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strict \(K\)-affinoid rigid spaces, and let
\[
                         q:V\longrightarrow U
\]
be a covering for the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology.  Write
\(U^{\mathrm B}\) and \(V^{\mathrm B}\) for the associated Berkovich
spaces.  If \(g:U^{\mathrm B}\to\mathbf R\) is continuous and
\(g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL, then \(g\) is
\(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{lemma}

% Exact theorem dependency needed by the P06.1 v2 candidate.
% The unrelated integral/rational-PL counterexample is intentionally absent.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, and let \(X\) be a good, strict, quasi-smooth \(K\)-analytic space.
Then every classically pluriharmonic function
\[
                             h:X\longrightarrow\mathbf R
\]
is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Equivalently, \(h\) is G-locally a finite real
linear combination of functions \(\log|f|\), with \(f\) an analytic unit.
Moreover, \(h\) is harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.  No global quasicompactness, separatedness, or
boundarylessness hypothesis is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-v3-single-shilov-factorization}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field. Let
\[
 p:W\longrightarrow V,
 \qquad s:V\longrightarrow W,
 \qquad p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_V
\]
be morphisms of good \(K\)-analytic spaces, with \(W\) and \(V\)
affinoid. Assume that every analytic fibre
\[
                    W_b=W\widehat\otimes_V\mathscr H(b),
                    \qquad b\in V,
\]
is nonempty and has singleton Shilov boundary. Then every classically
pluriharmonic function \(h\) on an ordinary open neighbourhood of \(W\)
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-single-shilov-factorization}
                         h|_W=p^*(s^*h).
\end{equation}
This proposition is a factorization statement only; it makes no
piecewise-linearity assertion.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-v3-single-shilov-rpl}
In addition to the hypotheses of
\cref{prop:p061-v3-single-shilov-factorization}, assume that \(K\) is
nontrivially valued and that \(W\) and \(V\) are good strictly
\(K\)-analytic spaces. If \(s^*h\) is locally \(\mathbf R\)-PL on \(V\),
then \(h|_W\) is locally \(\mathbf R\)-PL. In particular, this holds when
every classically pluriharmonic function on \(V\) is locally
\(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p061-v3-contractive-standard-etale-tube}
Let \(K\) be complete and nontrivially valued. Let
\[
                         B\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow B
\]
be homomorphisms of strict \(K\)-affinoid algebras whose composite is the
identity, and put \(J=\ker(A\to B)\). Let \((A_n)_{n\geq1}\) be strict
affinoid \(B\)-algebras with compatible maps
\[
                         A\longrightarrow A_n\longrightarrow B
\]
extending \(A\to B\). Choose admissible Banach norms for which all four
structural maps \(B\to A\), \(A\to B\), \(A\to A_n\), and
\(A_n\to B\) are contractions.

Suppose that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-standard-etale-presentation}
 C=A\langle T,U\rangle/
       \bigl(g(T),h(T)U-1\bigr),
\end{equation}
where \(g\in A[T]\) is monic and \(g'(T)\) is invertible in \(C\).
Give \(C\) its quotient Gauss norm. Let \(g_0,h_0\in B[T]\) be the
coefficientwise images. For every coefficient \(a\) of \(g\) or \(h\),
write
\[
                         a^\circ=a-\iota\varepsilon(a)\in J,
\]
where \(\varepsilon:A\to B\) and \(\iota:B\to A\) are the displayed
retraction and section. Assume
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-coefficient-contraction}
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \max_a\bigl\|a^\circ\bigr\|_{A_n}=0.
\end{equation}

Set
\[
 D=C\widehat\otimes_AB,
 \qquad C_n=C\widehat\otimes_AA_n,
 \qquad E_n=A_n\widehat\otimes_BD,
\]
identify the first two base changes with their canonical quotient Tate
presentations, give them the quotient Gauss norms, and give \(E_n\) the
projective tensor norm. Denote by \(t,u\) the images of
\(T,U\) in \(D\), and by \(T,U\) their images in \(C_n\). Then there are
one number \(0<r<1\) and one integer \(n_0\) such that, for every
\(n\geq n_0\), all four of the following assertions hold for that same
radius \(r\):
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(g\) has a unique zero \(t_n\) in the closed radius-\(r\) ball
 about \(t\) in \(E_n\);
\item \(g_0\) has \(t\) as its unique zero in that ball in \(E_n\);
\item \(g_0\) has a unique zero \(T_n^0\) in the closed radius-\(r\) ball
 about \(T\) in \(C_n\);
\item \(g\) has \(T\) as its unique zero in that ball in \(C_n\).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, \(h(t_n)\) and \(h_0(T_n^0)\) are invertible, with inverses of
norm at most one, and the assignments
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha_n:C_n&\longrightarrow E_n,
 &T&\longmapsto t_n,
 &U&\longmapsto h(t_n)^{-1},\\
 \beta_n:E_n&\longrightarrow C_n,
 &t&\longmapsto T_n^0,
 &u&\longmapsto h_0(T_n^0)^{-1}
 \end{aligned}
\]
are inverse contractive \(A_n\)-homomorphisms. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-etale-tube-isomorphism}
                         C_n\simeq E_n,
\end{equation}
and its reduction along \(A_n\to B\) is the identity of \(D\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-v3-etale-toric-product}
Let \(K\) be complete and nontrivially valued. Let \(N\) be a lattice,
let \(\rho\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be a full-dimensional strongly convex
rational polyhedral cone, and set
\[
 S=\rho^\vee\cap N^\vee,
 \qquad Z=\operatorname{Spec}K[S].
\]
Let \(a\in Z(K)\) be the torus-fixed point, let \(\mathcal Y\) be a
smooth \(K\)-variety, and let
\[
 q:\mathcal X\longrightarrow Z\times_K\mathcal Y
\]
be a separated etale morphism of finite-type \(K\)-schemes. Fix
\[
 x\in\mathcal X^{\mathrm{an}},
 \qquad q^{\mathrm{an}}(x)=(a,y).
\]
Then there are a strict affinoid neighbourhood \(V\) of \(y\) in
\(\mathcal Y^{\mathrm{an}}\), a strict affinoid neighbourhood \(D\) of
\(x\) in the fixed fibre
\[
 \mathcal X_a^{\mathrm{an}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal X\times_{Z\times\mathcal Y}
        (\{a\}\times\mathcal Y)\bigr)^{\mathrm{an}},
\]
a weighted strict toric affinoid neighbourhood \(U\) of \(a\), and a
strict affinoid neighbourhood \(\Omega\) of \(x\) in
\(\mathcal X^{\mathrm{an}}\), together with an isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-actual-product}
                            \Omega\simeq U\times_KD
\end{equation}
over \(U\times_KV\). Under this isomorphism the fixed fibre is
\(\{a\}\times D\). The space \(D\) is quasi-smooth, and every analytic
fibre of the projection \(\Omega\to D\) has singleton Shilov boundary.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-v3-etale-toroidal-ph-rpl}
In the setting of \cref{prop:p061-v3-etale-toric-product}, every
classically pluriharmonic function on an ordinary open neighbourhood of
\(x\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic on a smaller
ordinary open neighbourhood of \(x\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p061-v3-zariski-etale-toric-charts}
Let \(K\) be complete and nontrivially valued. Let \(\mathcal X\) be a
separated finite-type \(K\)-scheme admitting, Zariski locally on the
source, ordinary etale charts to the product of a split toric
\(K\)-variety and a smooth \(K\)-variety. Then every classically
pluriharmonic function on every ordinary open analytic subspace of
\(\mathcal X^{\mathrm{an}}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{lem:p061-product-open-tube}]
Let
\[
 \epsilon=\epsilon_a\widehat\otimes1:P\longrightarrow B.
\]
We first record the elementary uniform estimate used below.  If
\(G\in\ker\epsilon\) and \(\eta>0\), there is a strict affinoid
neighbourhood \(U\) of \(a\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-product-kernel-small}
       \sup_{U\times_K\mathcal M(B)}|G|<\eta.
\end{equation}
Indeed, choose a finite tensor
\(T=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\otimes b_i\) sufficiently close to \(G\), and put
\[
                  b_0=\epsilon(T)\in B.
\]
Boundedness of \(\epsilon\) and the equality \(\epsilon(G)=0\) make
\(\lVert b_0\rVert\) arbitrarily small with the approximation error.
Replacing \(T\) by
\[
 T-1\otimes b_0
   =\sum_{i=1}^r(a_i-a_i(a))\otimes b_i
\]
therefore still gives an arbitrarily close approximation.  Every
\(a_i-a_i(a)\) vanishes at
\(a\).  Nontriviality of the valuation supplies arbitrarily small strict
rational neighbourhoods on which all of them have the required small
supremum norm.  The ultrametric inequality proves
\eqref{eq:p061-product-kernel-small}.

Choose a basic ordinary neighbourhood of \(s_a(z)\), contained in
\(\Omega\), of the form
\[
 \Omega_0=
 \bigcap_{i=1}^r\{|F_i|<c_i\}
 \cap
 \bigcap_{j=1}^s\{|H_j|>d_j\},
 \qquad F_i,H_j\in P.
\]
Choose numbers
\[
 |\epsilon(F_i)(z)|<c_i'<c_i,
 \qquad
 d_j<d_j'<|\epsilon(H_j)(z)|.
\]
After shrinking to one strict affinoid neighbourhood \(V\) of \(z\), the
same strict inequalities hold throughout \(V\).  Write, for every
\(L\in\{F_i,H_j\}\),
\[
        L=1\otimes\epsilon(L)+
          \bigl(L-1\otimes\epsilon(L)\bigr).
\]
The second summand belongs to \(\ker\epsilon\).  Apply
\eqref{eq:p061-product-kernel-small} simultaneously, with error smaller
than \(c_i\) for \(F_i\) and smaller than \(d_j'\) for \(H_j\).  On the
resulting \(U\times_KV\), the upper inequalities follow from the
ultrametric triangle inequality.  In the lower inequalities the error is
strictly smaller than \(|\epsilon(H_j)|\), so
\[
                     |H_j|=|\epsilon(H_j)|>d_j'>d_j.
\]
Thus \(U\times_KV\subset\Omega_0\subset\Omega\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}]
Choose \(0<|\varpi|<1\) and
\(v\in N\cap\operatorname{int}(\rho)\), and put
\(\ell(u)=\langle u,v\rangle\).  The weighted domains \(U_n\) in
\eqref{eq:p061-parameterized-weighted-domain} are strict affinoid
neighbourhoods of \(a\): for finite monoid generators
\(u_1,\ldots,u_r\) of \(S\), the corresponding monomials give a closed
immersion \(Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf A_K^r\), and \(U_n\) is the inverse
image of the strict closed polydisc
\[
             |\chi^{u_i}|\leq
             |\varpi|^{n\ell(u_i)}
             \qquad(1\leq i\leq r).
\]
After rescaling the generators, their affinoid algebras are
\(K\langle S\rangle\) with the semigroup Gauss norm.  They are nested,
and
\[
                         \bigcap_{n\geq1}U_n=\{a\}.
\]
The compactness argument for nested closed subsets shows that they are
cofinal among ordinary neighbourhoods of \(a\).  More explicitly, if an
ordinary neighbourhood \(E\) of \(a\) contained no \(U_n\), the nonempty
closed subsets \(U_n\setminus E\) of the compact space \(U_1\) would have
nonempty intersection, contradicting the displayed identity.

Choose strict affinoid neighbourhoods \(A_0\) of \(a\) in
\(Z^{\mathrm{an}}\) and \(B_0\) of \(y\) in \(Y\).  By
\Cref{lem:p061-product-open-tube}, after shrinking there are strict
affinoid neighbourhoods \(A_1\subset A_0\) and \(V\subset B_0\) such
that
\[
                         A_1\times_KV\subset\Omega.
\]
Since \(A_1\) is a neighbourhood of \(a\), choose \(n\) with
\(U_n\subset A_1\).  It remains to prove that \(h\) is constant on every
fibre of
\[
                    p_V:U_n\times_KV\longrightarrow V.
\]
We do this over the actual completed residue field of an arbitrary point,
so no density or rigid-point argument is hidden.  Fix \(b\in V\).  The
analytic fibre is
\[
 (U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}=
 U_n\widehat\otimes_K\mathscr H(b).
\]
After the rescaling
\(Z^u=\varpi^{-n\ell(u)}\chi^u\), its affinoid algebra is the semigroup
Tate algebra
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-basechanged-semigroup-tate}
 \mathscr H(b)\langle S\rangle=
 \left\{\sum_{u\in S}c_uZ^u:
 c_u\in\mathscr H(b),\ |c_u|\longrightarrow0
 \text{ off finite subsets of }S\right\}
\end{equation}
with Gauss norm \(\max_u|c_u|\).  The Gauss norm is multiplicative: after
normalizing two nonzero series to norm one, their nonzero reductions have
nonzero product in the domain
\(\widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[S]\subset
 \widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[M]\).  It is therefore the supremum norm, and
the canonical reduction of \eqref{eq:p061-basechanged-semigroup-tate} is
\[
                       \widetilde{\mathscr H(b)}[S].
\]
This is an integral domain.  Hence
the Gauss norm defines a point \(\eta_{n,b}\) of
\((U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}\), and
\[
        |f(\eta_{n,b})|=\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm G}
                       =\sup_{(U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}}|f|
        \qquad
        \bigl(f\in\mathscr H(b)\langle S\rangle\bigr).
\]
Thus \(\{\eta_{n,b}\}\) is itself a boundary.  The nonempty minimal
Shilov boundary is consequently the singleton
\(\{\eta_{n,b}\}\).

First extend \(h\) from \(K\) to \(\mathscr H(b)\); this preserves
classical pluriharmonicity in both directions by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}.  The point \(b\) induces an
\(\mathscr H(b)\)-rational point of \(V_{\mathscr H(b)}\), and the
corresponding fibre inclusion
\[
 (U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}
 \longrightarrow (U_n\times_KV)_{\mathscr H(b)}
\]
is an \(\mathscr H(b)\)-analytic morphism.  Arbitrary pullback preserves
classical pluriharmonicity by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(7)]{GR25Classical}.  Thus the resulting pullback
\(h_b\) is pluriharmonic on the fibre.  The affinoid maximum--minimum
principle \cite[Proposition~7.3]{GR25Classical} says that both extrema of
\(h_b\) occur on its singleton Shilov boundary, so \(h_b\) is constant.
By the standard description of analytic fibres
\cite[\S2.7]{GR25Classical}, the underlying topological space of
\((U_n)_{\mathscr H(b)}\) identifies with the set-theoretic fibre
\(p_V^{-1}(b)\).  Hence every point of \(U_n\times_KV\) belongs to
exactly one of the analytic fibres just treated.  Its value under \(h\)
consequently equals the value at the toric-fixed section in that fibre.
This proves the pointwise identity
\[
              h|_{U_n\times_KV}=p_V^*(s_a^*h|_V).
\]
The function \(g=s_a^*h|_V\) is classically pluriharmonic by the same
functorial pullback result.  If pluriharmonic functions on \(Y\) are locally
\(\mathbf R\)-PL, shrink \(V\) once more and apply pullback stability of
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26}.  For quasi-smooth \(Y\), the required
regularity is the already verified quasi-smooth P06.1 theorem.  This
proves every assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits}]
Fix \(x\in W\).  There is a unique face
\(\tau\preceq\sigma\) such that \(x\in O(\tau)^{\mathrm{an}}\).  Put
\[
 N_\tau=N\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\tau).
\]
It is a saturated sublattice of \(N\), so choose a splitting
\(N=N_\tau\oplus N'\).  Choose
\[
 q\in\operatorname{relint}
 (\sigma^\vee\cap\tau^\perp)\cap M.
\]
Such an integral relative-interior point exists because the dual face is
rational polyhedral.  Since
\(\sigma\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\tau)=\tau\), its zero face
on \(\sigma\) is exactly \(\tau\).  Thus \(q\) vanishes on \(\tau\) and
is strictly positive on every ray of \(\sigma\) not contained in
\(\tau\).  The principal toric open
\(D(\chi^q)\) contains \(O(\tau)\).  Its monoid is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-localized-toric-monoid}
 (\sigma^\vee\cap M)+\mathbf Z(-q)
   =\{m\in M: m|_\tau\geq0\}.
\end{equation}
For completeness, the inclusion from left to right is immediate.  For
the converse, evaluate \(m\) on the finitely many primitive ray
generators of \(\sigma\).  It is nonnegative on those in \(\tau\), while
\(q\) is positive on all the others.  Hence \(m+r q\in\sigma^\vee\) for
all sufficiently large integers \(r\), which proves
\eqref{eq:p061-localized-toric-monoid}.

Dualizing the chosen lattice splitting identifies the monoid on the
right with
\[
 (\tau^\vee\cap N_\tau^\vee)\oplus (N')^\vee.
\]
Consequently there is an algebraic isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-orbit-product-chart}
 D(\chi^q)\simeq
 X_{\tau,N_\tau}\times_K T_{N'},
\end{equation}
under which \(O(\tau)\) is the product of the torus-fixed point of
\(X_{\tau,N_\tau}\) and the split torus \(T_{N'}\).  Notice that
\(\tau\) is full-dimensional in \((N_\tau)_{\mathbf R}\), whether or not
it is simplicial.

Under \eqref{eq:p061-orbit-product-chart}, the point \(x\) has the form
\((a,y)\), with \(a\) the rational fixed point and
\(y\in T_{N'}^{\mathrm{an}}\).  The set
\(W\cap D(\chi^q)^{\mathrm{an}}\) is an ordinary open neighbourhood of
\((a,y)\).  Apply
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}.  It factors \(h\), on
a product affinoid neighbourhood of \(x\), as the pullback of a
classically pluriharmonic function on a strict affinoid domain of the
split torus.  The torus is quasi-smooth, so the verified quasi-smooth
P06.1 theorem makes that function \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Pullback stability
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26} makes \(h\) \(\mathbf R\)-PL near \(x\).

Since \(x\) was arbitrary and \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions form a sheaf
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}, \(h\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL on \(W\).  Both \(h\)
and \(-h\) are classically psh.  On a good strict analytic space,
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} identifies classical psh
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions with semipositive ones.  Thus both signs are
semipositive, which is harmonicity in
\cite[Definition~7.2]{GJR26}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties}]
A split toric variety is covered by the affine toric opens attached to
the cones of its fan.  The first assertion therefore follows from
\Cref{thm:p061-split-toric-all-orbits} and sheafiness.  In the second
assertion, transfer a classically pluriharmonic function through the
given analytic local isomorphism and apply
\Cref{prop:p061-parameterized-toric-fixed-fibre}.  The quasi-smooth
P06.1 theorem applies to the \(Y\)-factor, and pullback through the local
isomorphism returns the claimed \(\mathbf R\)-PL and harmonic germ.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{cor:p061-toric-forms}]
Let \(\pi:X_L^{\mathrm{an}}\to X^{\mathrm{an}}\) be the scalar-extension
map.  Extension of scalars preserves classical pluriharmonicity in both
directions by \cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}.  Thus the pullback
of the given function is classically pluriharmonic on the inverse image
of the ordinary open subspace.  This inverse image is an ordinary open
subspace of the split toric variety \(X_L^{\mathrm{an}}\), so
\Cref{cor:p061-split-toric-varieties} makes the pullback
\(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Ground-field descent for \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions
\cite[Corollary~5.12]{GJR26} gives the assertion over \(K\).

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent}]
Work on the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale site \(U_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\) of
de Jong--van der Put.  For an object \(W\to U\), define \(\mathscr P(W)\)
to be the compatible families of \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions on all strict
affinoid G-domains of \(W\).  Thus it is the space of global sections of
the affinoid-local G-sheaf
\[
 A\longmapsto\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(A^{\mathrm B}).
\]
When \(W\) is affinoid, this is
\(\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W^{\mathrm B})\).  This definition covers
all, including globally nongood, objects of the rigid
\(\acute{e}\)tale site.  Pullback makes \(\mathscr P\) a presheaf: on good
strict Berkovich spaces this is
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26}, and the general rigid object follows by the
affinoid-local definition.

We verify the two conditions of
\cite[Proposition~3.2.2]{dJvdP96}.  First, the restriction of
\(\mathscr P\) to every rigid G-site is a sheaf by construction and
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}.  The special rigid G-topology used by
de Jong--van der Put has the same category of sheaves as the usual strong
rigid G-topology by \cite[\S2.1]{dJvdP96}, so there is no change of sheaf
category in this step.

For the second condition, let \(f:W'\to W\) be a surjective finite
\(\acute{e}\)tale morphism of strict affinoid rigid spaces.  We prove
exactness of
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer}
  0\longrightarrow\mathscr P(W)\longrightarrow\mathscr P(W')
  \mathrel{\substack{\longrightarrow\\[-0.6ex]\longrightarrow}}
  \mathscr P(W'\times_W W').
\end{equation}
For clarity, \(f^{\mathrm B}\) is surjective: finite
\(\acute{e}\)taleness and surjectivity make the affinoid algebra map finite
faithfully flat, so its base change to \(\mathscr H(x)\) is a nonzero finite
algebra for every \(x\in W^{\mathrm B}\), and any maximal-ideal quotient
supplies a point above \(x\).  Injectivity in
\eqref{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer} follows.  Now take
\(s'\in\mathscr P(W')\) whose two pullbacks to \(W'\times_WW'\) agree.
We first show that \(s'\) is constant on every Berkovich fibre.  Let
\(y_1,y_2\in (W')^{\mathrm B}\) have common image
\(x\in W^{\mathrm B}\).  Since \(f\) is finite, each
\(\mathscr H(y_i)\) is a finite separable extension of \(\mathscr H(x)\).
Choose a common finite, hence complete, valued extension \(\Omega\) of
\(\mathscr H(x)\) and \(\mathscr H(x)\)-embeddings
\(\iota_i:\mathscr H(y_i)\hookrightarrow\Omega\).  The embeddings are
isometric because the absolute value has a unique extension to a finite
extension of a complete non-Archimedean field.  The bounded homomorphism
\[
 \mathscr H(y_1)\widehat\otimes_{\mathscr H(x)}\mathscr H(y_2)
 \longrightarrow\Omega,\qquad
 a\otimes b\longmapsto\iota_1(a)\iota_2(b),
\]
followed by the absolute value of \(\Omega\), is a bounded multiplicative
seminorm.  Its restriction to each factor is exactly the prescribed absolute
value defining \(y_i\), by the isometry just noted.  It therefore gives a
point \(z\) of
\((W'\times_WW')^{\mathrm B}\) whose two projections are \(y_1\) and
\(y_2\).  Equality of the two pullbacks at \(z\) gives
\(s'(y_1)=s'(y_2)\).

There is therefore a unique function \(s:W^{\mathrm B}\to\mathbf R\)
such that \(s'=s\circ f^{\mathrm B}\).  Both Berkovich affinoid spaces are
compact Hausdorff.  Thus the continuous surjection \(f^{\mathrm B}\) is
closed and is a quotient map.  Since \(s'\) is continuous, the defining
property of the quotient topology shows that \(s\) is continuous.  A
finite \(\acute{e}\)tale morphism is finite, flat, and surjective, so
\cite[Proposition~5.11]{GJR26}, applied with the divisible coefficient
group \(\mathbf R\), shows from
\(s'=f^*s\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W')\) that
\(s\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W)\).  This proves the equalizer
condition \eqref{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer}.

The criterion \cite[Proposition~3.2.2]{dJvdP96} now says that
\(\mathscr P\) is a sheaf for the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology.  The
section \(g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\) belongs to \(\mathscr P(V)\), and its two
pullbacks to \(V\times_UV\) agree because it is pulled back from the
function \(g\).  Sheaf descent supplies a section \(s\in\mathscr P(U)\)
with \(s\circ q^{\mathrm B}=g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\).  The covering map is
surjective, so \(s=g\).  Hence \(g\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl}]
Fix \(x\in X\).  Goodness and strictness give a strict affinoid
neighbourhood \(U\) of \(x\).  Quasi-smoothness is preserved on analytic
domains.  Under the rigid--Berkovich equivalence recalled in
\cite[\S3.4]{Temkin17}, let \(\mathcal U\) be the rigid space associated to
\(U\); it is smooth, quasicompact, and quasiseparated, and
\(\mathcal U^{\mathrm B}=U\).

Apply \cite[Corollary~3.3.2]{Temkin17}.  There are a finite extension
\(L/K\) and a covering in the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology
\[
                 q:\mathcal V\longrightarrow\mathcal U_L
\]
such that \(\mathcal V\) is affinoid and possesses a strictly semistable
affine formal \(L^\circ\)-model.  This is the precise version needed below.
In particular, we do not replace it by the wording of
\cite[Theorem~3.4.1]{Temkin17}, and we do not assert that \(q\) itself is
finite or flat.

Let \(h_U=h|_U\).  The scalar extension \((h_U)_L\) is classically
pluriharmonic on \(\mathcal U_L^{\mathrm B}\) by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}, and hence is continuous by the
opening assertion of that proposition.  Its pullback
\((q^{\mathrm B})^*(h_U)_L\) is classically pluriharmonic by the
arbitrary-morphism
direction of \cite[Proposition~7.2(7)]{GR25Classical}; relative boundary of
the associated quasi-\(\acute{e}\)tale Berkovich morphism causes no problem
for this functorial statement.

The space \(\mathcal V^{\mathrm B}\) is good, quasicompact, and strict and
has the strictly semistable formal model just supplied.  Therefore
\cite[Proposition~7.8]{GR25Classical} gives
\[
                   (q^{\mathrm B})^*(h_U)_L\in
                   \operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal V^{\mathrm B}).
\]
The complete \(\acute{e}\)tale descent in
\Cref{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent} now gives
\((h_U)_L\in
\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal U_L^{\mathrm B})\).  Since \(L/K\)
is finite, it is already complete and is the completion of an algebraic
extension.  Ground-field descent
\cite[Corollary~5.12]{GJR26}, again with coefficient group \(\mathbf R\),
gives
\(h_U\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal U^{\mathrm B})
=\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(U)\).

Every point \(x\in X\) has such a neighbourhood \(U\), and
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions form a G-sheaf by
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}.  Hence
\(h\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X)\).

Finally, both \(h\) and \(-h\) are classically psh by definition.  For an
\(\mathbf R\)-PL function on a good strict space,
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} identifies classical psh with
semipositivity.  Thus both signs of \(h\) are semipositive, which is exactly
harmonicity in \cite[Definition~7.2]{GJR26}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of
\cref{lem:p061-v3-contractive-standard-etale-tube}]
Completed tensor product commutes with these finite Tate presentations and
their closed ideals. With the norms specified in the statement, the quotient
presentation gives
\[
 D=B\langle t,u\rangle/
       \bigl(g_0(t),h_0(t)u-1\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-exact-central-relations}
 g_0(t)=0,
 \qquad h_0(t)u=1,
 \qquad \|t\|_D\leq1,
 \qquad \|u\|_D\leq1.
\end{equation}
Likewise \(\|T\|_{C_n},\|U\|_{C_n}\leq1\). The canonical maps
\(C\to C_n\) and \(D\to E_n\) are contractions for these quotient and
projective norms.

We first isolate a quantitative Banach estimate. Let \(R\) be a
non-Archimedean Banach algebra, let \(F\in R[X]\), and suppose
\(F'(z)\) is invertible. Write
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-taylor-expansion}
 F(z+X)=F(z)+F'(z)X+\sum_{j=2}^{d}c_jX^j.
\end{equation}
If \(M\geq\|F'(z)^{-1}\|\), \(H\geq\max_{j\geq2}\|c_j\|\), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-newton-inequalities}
                 MH r<1,
 \qquad \|F'(z)^{-1}F(z)\|\leq r,
\end{equation}
then
\[
 \Phi(\delta)=
 -F'(z)^{-1}F(z)
 -F'(z)^{-1}\sum_{j=2}^{d}c_j\delta^j
\]
is a strict contraction of the closed radius-\(r\) ball. Indeed, it maps
the ball to itself by the ultrametric inequality, and
\[
 \|\Phi(\delta)-\Phi(\delta')\|
 \leq MH r\,\|\delta-\delta'\|,
\]
because \(r<1\) and
\(\|\delta^j-(\delta')^j\|\leq
r^{j-1}\|\delta-\delta'\|\). Its unique fixed point gives the unique zero
of \(F\) in that ball. This also proves uniqueness directly: every zero in
the ball is a fixed point of \(\Phi\).

We now choose constants uniformly for all four root problems. The fixed
inverses
\[
                  g'(T)^{-1}\in C,
 \qquad g_0'(t)^{-1}\in D
\]
have bounded images in \(C_n\) and \(E_n\). Put
\[
 M=\max\bigl\{1,\|g'(T)^{-1}\|_C,
                    \|g_0'(t)^{-1}\|_D\bigr\}.
\]
The coefficient-contraction hypothesis and
\(\|t\|,\|T\|\leq1\) give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-polynomial-errors}
 \begin{aligned}
  \|g(t)\|_{E_n}&\longrightarrow0,&
  \|g'(t)-g_0'(t)\|_{E_n}&\longrightarrow0,\\
  \|g_0(T)\|_{C_n}&\longrightarrow0,&
  \|g_0'(T)-g'(T)\|_{C_n}&\longrightarrow0,\\
  \|h(t)-h_0(t)\|_{E_n}&\longrightarrow0,&
  \|h_0(T)-h(T)\|_{C_n}&\longrightarrow0.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
After increasing \(n\), the two perturbed derivatives are invertible by
the Neumann series and all four derivative inverses have norm at most
\(M\).

Taylor expansion of \(g\) and \(g_0\) at \(t\) and at \(T\) produces
only finitely many coefficient expressions. Contractivity of every
structural map and the unit bounds on the two centres therefore give one
number \(H\geq1\) bounding every higher Taylor coefficient in all four
expansions, uniformly in \(n\); enlarge \(H\), if necessary, to cover the
fixed expansion of \(g_0\) at \(t\) in \(D\) as well. Similarly, there is
one \(L\geq1\) such
that both \(h\) and \(h_0\) are \(L\)-Lipschitz on each closed unit ball
appearing below.

Choose, once and for all,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-common-radius}
          0<r<1,
 \qquad M H r<1,
 \qquad Lr<1.
\end{equation}
Then increase \(n\) once more so that the two derivative perturbations
above are Neumann-small and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-v3-common-error-bound}
 \begin{aligned}
 \|g'(t)^{-1}g(t)\|_{E_n}&\leq r,&
 \|g_0'(T)^{-1}g_0(T)\|_{C_n}&\leq r,\\
 \|h(t)-h_0(t)\|_{E_n}&<1,&
 \|h_0(T)-h(T)\|_{C_n}&<1.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}

Apply \eqref{eq:p061-v3-newton-inequalities} with this single \(r\) to
the following four triples:
\[
 (E_n,g,t),
 \qquad (E_n,g_0,t),
 \qquad (C_n,g_0,T),
 \qquad (C_n,g,T).
\]
For the first and third triples, \eqref{eq:p061-v3-polynomial-errors}
gives the required small Newton error and produces \(t_n\) and \(T_n^0\).
For the second and fourth triples the centre is already an exact root, so
the unique root is respectively \(t\) and \(T\). This proves, with an
actual common radius, all four uniqueness assertions in the statement.
The same estimate in \(D\) also makes \(t\) the unique zero of \(g_0\)
in its radius-\(r\) ball; this will be used after reduction.

The ultrametric inequality, the unit bounds on the centres, and \(r<1\)
give \(\|t_n\|_{E_n},\|T_n^0\|_{C_n}\leq1\). The localization factors have
the required bounds. For example,
\[
 \|h(t_n)-h_0(t)\|_{E_n}
 \leq\max\bigl\{L\|t_n-t\|,
                  \|h(t)-h_0(t)\|\bigr\}<1.
\]
Since \(u=h_0(t)^{-1}\) and \(\|u\|\leq1\), the element
\(h(t_n)=h_0(t)(1+u(h(t_n)-h_0(t)))\) is invertible and
\(\|h(t_n)^{-1}\|\leq1\). The same calculation with
\(U=h(T)^{-1}\) gives \(\|h_0(T_n^0)^{-1}\|\leq1\).

The universal property of the unit-radius Tate algebra now gives a
contractive \(A_n\)-homomorphism
\[
 \alpha_n:C_n\longrightarrow E_n,
 \qquad T\longmapsto t_n,
 \qquad U\longmapsto h(t_n)^{-1}.
\]
The displayed relations show that it factors through \(C_n\). Likewise,
the unit bounds define a contractive \(B\)-homomorphism
\[
 D\longrightarrow C_n,
 \qquad t\longmapsto T_n^0,
 \qquad u\longmapsto h_0(T_n^0)^{-1}.
\]
Together with \(A_n\to C_n\), the universal property of
\(A_n\widehat\otimes_BD\) gives the contractive
\(A_n\)-homomorphism \(\beta_n:E_n\to C_n\).

We use the two exact-root uniqueness statements, not merely the two
existence statements, to identify the composites. Since \(\alpha_n\) is

\[

 \leq\max\bigl\{\|T_n^0-T\|_{C_n},
                  \|t_n-t\|_{E_n}\bigr\}\leq r.
\]
The element \(\alpha_n(T_n^0)\) is a zero of \(g_0\), so assertion (2)
gives \(\alpha_n\beta_n(t)=t\). Similarly,
\[
 \|\beta_n(t_n)-T\|_{C_n}
 \leq\max\bigl\{\|t_n-t\|_{E_n},
                  \|T_n^0-T\|_{C_n}\bigr\}\leq r,
\]
and \(\beta_n(t_n)\) is a zero of \(g\); assertion (4) gives

\(U\), and both composites already fix \(A_n\). These elements
topologically generate the two quotient Tate algebras, hence
\(\alpha_n\) and \(\beta_n\) are inverse.

Finally tensor the construction through \(A_n\to B\). The coefficient
errors vanish, and the image of \(t_n\) is a zero of \(g_0\) within
distance \(r\) of \(t\). The uniqueness estimate in \(D\) makes it
equal to \(t\); the localization inverse then equals \(u\). The same
argument applies to \(T_n^0\). Thus the reduced isomorphism is the
identity of \(D\).
\end{proof}
